Masters are kept in three places: on the workroom computer, on the external disk in the strong
room safe, and on the disk that the treasurer keeps at home. The two disks are swapped on the first
Saturday of the month at the same time as the water alarm is tested, and the swap is signed on the
same sheet, by the same hand, at the same time. Storage that lives in a single place is not storage but
a hope, and the archive lost the whole of its first year of scanning in 2009 by hoping rather than

Scans are made at the resolution written on the card by the scanner, saved in the uncompressed
master format, and named by reference number followed by a sequence number. A derived copy at
reading size is made for the catalogue. The master is never edited, cropped or rotated after capture;
if it is wrong, it is rescanned. Corrections to a master are the digital equivalent of writing on the
original and are treated with exactly the same seriousness by everyone, without exception. Scans are made at the resolution written on the card by the scanner, saved in the uncompressed
